approval-path.title: Approval-path attacks from Kodathala, Pollishetty and Cargill, arXiv:2610.21063 (draft for review)

vectors.name: approved-payment-executed-as-approved
vectors.question: Alice approves this exact payment, and the bank executes exactly that.

vectors.name: signed-body-with-both-amounts-is-preserved
vectors.note: Shows the limit of after-the-fact evidence: if the signed bytes contain the attack, the approval is genuine. Detection then depends on trusted rendering (the paper's H3), not on the evidence.
vectors.question: Alice's key signed a body that really contains both amounts. The evidence binds what was signed; whether the card showed both amounts is outside what evidence can show.

vectors.name: small-payment-within-budget-needs-no-approval
vectors.question: One payment within the mandate's risk budget; no approval is required.

vectors.name: two-payments-two-approvals
vectors.question: Two payments, each with its own approval, each used once.

vectors.name: amount-cancellation
vectors.question: Alice approved a net 50 EUR; the executed body carries +5,000 and -4,950.

vectors.name: approval-marked-consumed
vectors.question: The approval record is already marked consumed when it is presented.

vectors.name: approval-replayed-in-same-run
vectors.question: One approval is cited by two payments with identical bodies: one response, two executions.

vectors.name: approval-reused-for-larger-amount
vectors.question: An approval for 1,200 EUR is presented for a 1,900 EUR payment to the same payee.

vectors.name: approval-signed-by-enrolled-attacker-key
vectors.note: Unresolved, not violated: the evidence cannot show who controls the unknown key, only that no authorised approver signed. Detection depends on the verifier's key set being enrolled honestly.
vectors.question: The attacker enrolled its own passkey and approved its own call. The key holds no approver role in Alice's key set.

vectors.name: approval-used-after-expiry
vectors.question: The approval expired before the payment executed.

vectors.name: decoy-field-recipient
vectors.question: The approved body names the landlord; the executed body adds a second beneficiary under an innocuous key.

vectors.name: decoy-recipient-executed
vectors.note: Caught by I2 (declared differs from executed) before the approval check is reached.
vectors.question: The agent declared and Alice approved a payment to the landlord; the bank's receipt shows the attacker was paid.

vectors.name: hidden-text-in-executed-argument
vectors.note: Only the case where the hidden text was added after approval. If Alice's key signed the hidden text, see AB4 under 'Not detectable from evidence' in README.md.
vectors.question: The executed memo contains a right-to-left override and padding that the approved body did not.

vectors.name: payment-split-under-threshold
vectors.note: AMEP budgets count effect cost units (here 60 per irreversible payment), not currency. A monetary threshold would need a profile; see README.md.
vectors.question: One large payment is split into two that each look small. The mandate's risk budget (100) is exceeded by the second, which carries no approval.

vectors.name: post-approval-substitution
vectors.question: Arguments change between approval and execution: Alice approved 1,200 EUR, the bank executed 12,000 EUR.

vectors.name: standing-grant-to-new-payee
vectors.question: A standing grant covers the landlord and the utility; the agent pays a new payee under it.
